recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-13462 unless a future work-group decision reopens Event occurrence Timing guidance or a broader editorial pass chooses to clean up non-semantic spelling/spacing.
issue_request: FHIR-13462 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I change request for STU3 asking to enhance Event.occurrence[x], especially for Timing, to distinguish actual event timing from requested timing, explain ongoing events through status and open Period/Timing.bounds, and caution that Timing is generally appropriate only for summary event resources.
initial_application: Historical git-svn commit 5064224bd079b7f4ef4023d3ead9111b57bd8bff, corresponding to SVN revision 12374 referenced in the Jira comment, added the resolved Event.occurrence[x] definition and usage paragraph to source/event/event-spreadsheet.xml.
additional_context: Event is an active logical pattern in source/fhir.ini, and source/event/event-spreadsheet.xml remains current build-scope source. A pickaxe search of the Event spreadsheet shows the upper-bound sentence was introduced by the 2017 application commit and has not been removed by later Event source edits. Related Timing-use decisions FHIR-12637 and FHIR-13231 support the same actual/requested and past/ongoing timing distinction. Targeted Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant conflicting record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Event.occurrence[x] row already includes dateTime|Period|Timing, the resolved definition, and the usage guidance about basedOn request timing, event status, open-ended ongoing events, and constrained Timing use. Remaining differences from Jira prose are templating and minor editorial artifacts rather than a semantic gap.
